the regularity of modules over commutative, graded algebras.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, if $R$ is not Kosul, then $R$ is a complete intersection if and only if all syzygies of $k$ have finite regularity.
the modules of infinite regularity in this setting are precisely the syzygies of $k$.
the vanishing of graded deviations of a graded commutative algebra over a field implies that all nonzero modules of finite regularity are syzygies of $k$.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, over a graded, commmutative algebra $R$, if the nonzero modules of finite regularity are not dense in the category $\mathrm{Mod}^{\infty}(R)$ of modules of infinite regularity then $R$ is Koszul.
the modules of infinite regularity behave in a similar way as the modules of finite regularity, but in the absence of Koszulity.

, if $R$ is a graded, commutive algebra over $k$ and $\mathfrak{n}$ is a graded ideal of $R$, we prove that if $\mathfrak n$ is not a Koszul ideal, then the regularity of $\mathfrak {n}$ and the regularity of $R$ are the same.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the regularity of a module is not a property of a module itself, but rather of the algebra it lives in, and that the regularity behaves differently for Koszul and non-Koszul rings.
the vanishing of graded deviations is a strong condition.
the regularity of a nonzero module over a non-Koszul graded ring tends to be infinite.
